summary: Telegram-controlled backdoor disguised as a Minecraft YouTube receiver
details: The package polls the Telegram Bot API on a loop using a base64-obfuscated bot token, chat id and topic id embedded in the module, and executes commands received from that chat on the installer's Windows host. Capabilities include downloading and running yt-dlp, ffmpeg and deno into %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\tools (a staging path chosen to blend with Windows crypto material), playing attacker-chosen videos fullscreen while blocking keyboard and mouse input via the `keyboard` and `pynput` libraries, killing explorer.exe to hide the taskbar, and force-shutting down the machine. The README advertises the package as a benign YouTube receiver for Minecraft and does not mention remote control. On import the module silently pip-installs `requests`, `keyboard`, `pynput` and `psutil` into the current interpreter with stdout/stderr redirected to devnull and CREATE_NO_WINDOW, so the dependencies required for the input-blocking and network channel are pulled in without user consent. The bot token, chat id, topic id and staging directory names are stored as base64 strings and reassembled at runtime via a helper `d(s)=base64.b64decode(s).decode()`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
